client_situation.text: The City of Colfax, California, a city of just under 2,000 residents in the Sierra Nevada foothills of Placer County, issued this RFP on July 1, 2025 for accounting and financial reporting software.
The City operates on a $6 million annual budgeted revenue base with 11 full-time employees (one position vacant) plus 1 part-time/seasonal/contract employee, and its fiscal year ends June 30.

The City currently runs Fund Balance fund accounting software from Tyler Technologies with modules for Accounts Payable (including 1099 filing, purchasing requisitions, and purchase orders with approvals), Accounts Receivable, General Ledger, Payroll, Utility Billing, and Business Licensing, used by five users.

The City wants a streamlined package that captures financial transactions systematically and efficiently, including budgeting and forecasting, and that supports data analysis for informed decision-making.
The City needs to maintain auditable records and documentation for future reference, and wants dedicated technical support during implementation and throughout annual contract renewals.

The City's stated goal is to go live on the new system by July 1, 2026, aligned with the start of its new fiscal year, which implies the current Tyler Technologies Fund Balance system must be replaced within roughly nine months of contract award.

goal.text: The City seeks a cloud-based accounting and financial reporting software system, including complete support for initial implementation and ongoing services for all applications the selected vendor provides.
The scope covers four tasks: approach and project management plan, software installation and implementation, staff training during implementation, and ongoing technical assistance and support.

Task 1 requires weekly progress/budget/timeline meetings, a dedicated project manager and technical staff, understanding of the City's auditing and reporting requirements, and a recommended account structure for auditable reporting.

Task 2 requires assistance with financial report writing, import of the prior five years of data for history, and collaboration with Accounting and IT to minimize disruption and downtime during transition.
Task 3 requires personalized training and manuals for power users, at least one recorded training session and manual for all staff, and support for the first 12 months post-implementation.
Task 4 requires automated updates and software change communications, support for annual e-filing such as 1099s and W-2s, and a help desk or ticketing system for prioritizing support.
The City intends to award a contract to a single respondent for all items, though it reserves the right to make separate awards, not award certain items, or cancel the RFP.

success_criteria.text: Proposals are scored on four weighted criteria: 45% response to project goals and scope, 25% technical support during implementation and ongoing, 20% fee proposal and implementation schedule, and 10% information, qualifications, and references.
Written questions must be submitted by July 31, 2025, with the City posting responses on www.colfax-ca.gov by August 14, 2025.
Proposals are due August 28, 2025 at 4:00 PM PST, with finalists notified September 11, 2025, virtual finalist interviews (if needed) on September 25, 2025, and contract award by October 22, 2025.

The City will confirm proposals meet the RFP's specifications and requirements before sending only qualified proposals to the selection committee, and may reject any proposal on the basis of fit, form, and function as well as cost.
Respondents must submit a completed Software Abilities and Requirements spreadsheet (Attachment F) and outline the availability of virtual demos to view product capabilities.
Respondents must provide at least three references for similar services with valid email addresses, and failure to provide a valid email may result in rejection of the proposal.
The City prefers at least one local referral available for an in-person software demonstration.

constraints.text: Proposals must not exceed 20 pages, with an additional two pages allowed for the cover letter and five pages for appendices, submitted as one signed original hard copy plus one digital version.

The digital copy and all attachments must be emailed to accounting@colfax-ca.gov by August 28, 2025 at 4:00 PM PST with the subject line "Accounting and Financial Software Submission," and the hard copy must arrive by the same deadline at Attn: Shanna Stahl, PO Box 702, Colfax, CA 95713 (USPS) or 33 S. Main Street, Colfax, CA 95713; late and FAX submissions will not be accepted.

The City will not accept unlimited reimbursable expenses, so any reimbursable expenses must be capped in the price proposal, and Attachment A requires a total price for all services and deliverables, a total reimbursable expenses cap, and a total price proposal.

Attachment C requires the Respondent to state whether any work will be performed outside the United States and, if so, list those locations and describe the corporate structure, which the City will evaluate for additional risks and costs before award.

Attachment G requires documentation of measures protecting financial data and the secure access controls implemented, and Attachment E requires proof of workers compensation and commercial general liability insurance.

Attachment D requires a signed Certification of Financial Condition covering an unqualified audit opinion, no outstanding IRS or government liabilities, current federal and state taxes, and no disqualifying litigation, with notice to the Contract Lead within 15 days of any material change.

The City rejects and will not evaluate additional or modified terms and conditions submitted with a proposal, and any attempt to alter or delete that paragraph is grounds to reject the proposal as nonresponsive; exceptions must instead be raised as questions by July 31, 2025.

The Software Abilities and Requirements spreadsheet (Attachment F) is a separate Excel document to be provided by the City and is not included in the RFP text, and the City's standard contract with terms and conditions is available only upon request, so bidders must obtain both.

chunk_summaries.summary: The document is a Request for Proposals issued by the CITY OF COLFAX for Accounting and Financial Reporting Software. Date of Issue: July 1, 2025. Submission Deadline: Thursday, August 28, 2025 at 4:00 PM PST. The chunk begins a section directing all inquiries concerning this RFP to a contact (contact details not included in this chunk).

The City of Colfax (City) is issuing this Request for Proposals (RFP) to solicit comprehensive proposals for the acquisition and implementation of a cloud-based accounting and financial reporting software system. The scope includes complete support for both initial implementation and ongoing services for all applications provided by the selected software vendor. Key objectives: a streamlined software package capturing financial transactions systematically and efficiently, including budgeting and forecasting capabilities; ability to generate reports and analyze data to support informed decision-making; ability to maintain auditable records and documentation for future reference; dedicated technical support during implementation and throughout annual contract renewals. The City currently uses Fund Balance fund accounting software from Tyler Technologies, with modules for Accounts Payable (with 1099 filing capability, purchasing requisitions, and purchase orders with approvals), Accounts Receivable, General Ledger, Payroll, Utility Billing, and Business Licensing, with currently five users.

The client is the City of Colfax, California, a small city in the Sierra Nevada foothills of Placer County with a population just under 2,000, located at the junction of Interstate 80 and State Route 174 between Sacramento and Lake Tahoe. The city was originally inhabited by the Maidu and Miwok peoples, gained prominence during the Gold Rush era, was named after Schuyler Colfax, and retains landmarks such as the restored 1905 Southern Pacific Railroad depot. Annual budgeted revenues are $6 million. The city has 11 full-time employees with one position vacant, plus 1 part-time/seasonal/contract employee. The fiscal-year end is June 30.

The RFP comprises the primary RFP document, any attachments, and any addenda issued prior to contract award. All attachments and addenda released in relation to this RFP before any contract award are incorporated by reference.

The RFP is issued by the City of Colfax, which states it will make every effort to adhere to the schedule. Schedule dates: RFP issued July 1, 2025; Respondents submit written questions by July 31, 2025; City of Colfax provides responses to questions on its website www.colfax-ca.gov by August 14, 2025; Respondents submit proposals by August 28, 2025; finalists notified September 11, 2025; virtual finalists' interviews (if needed) with Finalists & Colfax on September 25, 2025; selection and contract award by City of Colfax on October 22, 2025. The schedule is overseen by the Contract Lead.

Respondents may seek clarification of the RFP documents and must submit questions by the due date indicated in Section 2.2. Written inquiries must be emailed to accounting@colfax-ca.gov with the subject line "Accounting Software Proposal Questions," and must refer to the relevant RFP section. Questions received before the submission deadline, the City's responses, and any additional terms will be posted as an addendum on the City's website www.colfax-ca.gov; the addendum becomes part of the RFP. Only written material in an Addendum is considered authoritative and binding; informal or oral communications from City personnel are not official, and the City is bound only by the RFP and formal Addenda.

The City of Colfax urges all potential respondents to read the full RFP document and attachments before responding. Respondents bear all costs for preparing and submitting proposals or participating in interviews; the City will not reimburse these costs. The City will keep confidential trade secrets hidden as allowed by law; each page containing such information must be labeled "CONFIDENTIAL" at the top and bottom with the specific trade secret information enclosed. Cost information cannot be marked as confidential, and confidential markings must be limited as much as possible.

The client is the City of Colfax ("CITY"). The chunk defines terms used in the RFP: CONTRACT (agreement for services over a specified period at an agreed price); CONTRACT LEAD (City of Colfax representative who coordinates with Respondents for contracting and manages the contract); RFP (Request for Proposals); PROPOSAL (submission from a Respondent in response to the RFP); QUALIFIED PROPOSAL (a compliant proposal from a responsible Respondent meeting RFP requirements); RESPONDENT (entity submitting a response, e.g., supplier, company, firm, partnership, individual). IMPLEMENTATION is defined as the timeframe for installation, including planning, development, execution, and monitoring until software is fully operational, including expansions.

Respondents are responsible for reading the Instructions, the City's terms and conditions, all relevant exhibits and attachments, and any other components of this RFP, and for obtaining and complying with all addenda and other changes issued in connection with the RFP. A copy of the City's standard contract with terms and conditions is available upon request. Questions, issues or exceptions regarding any term, condition, instruction or other component must be submitted as questions per Section 2.3 Proposal Questions; if the City determines changes will be made, they will be communicated in an RFP addendum, and the City may leave open later negotiation and amendment of specific contract provisions addressed during the question-and-answer period. The City rejects and will not evaluate or consider any additional or modified terms and conditions or instructions submitted with a Respondent's proposal, and by submitting a proposal the Respondent agrees such additional or modified terms have no force or effect; noncompliance with or any attempt to alter or delete this paragraph is sufficient grounds to reject the proposal as nonresponsive.

The chunk sets rules on altering or deleting this paragraph: noncompliance or any attempt to alter or delete it is sufficient grounds to reject a proposal as nonresponsive. Respondents wanting modification of the solicitation's terms and conditions are urged to inquire during the question period per Section 2.3 whether specific proposed language is acceptable to or will be considered by the City. Objections or exceptions to the City's terms and conditions stated in the proposal itself are not allowed and will be disregarded or the proposal rejected. By submitting a proposal, the Respondent understands and agrees the City may exercise discretion not to consider any and all proposed modifications.

The City will evaluate all qualified proposals submitted by the due date; selection is based on the criteria in Section 3.4: Evaluation Criteria. The goal is to award a contract to a single respondent for all items, but the City may make separate awards for different items, not award certain items, or cancel the RFP entirely. The City reserves the right to waive minor informalities or technicalities in received proposals.

From proposal submission to contract award, respondents (including representatives, sub-contractors, and suppliers) must not communicate with anyone inside or outside relevant agencies or private entities about their own or others' proposals or qualifications. Violation of this rule leads to disqualification unless the City deems the communication harmless and unintentional and in the City's best interest. Exceptions are authorized communications by the issuing agency and general inquiries before submission and after status updates.

The City shall review all proposals to confirm they meet the RFP's specifications and requirements; only qualified proposals are sent to the selection committee for evaluation. The City reserves the right to reject any proposal on the basis of fit, form, and function as well as cost, and all information furnished in the proposal may be used in determining contract award. Qualified proposals are assessed according to the evaluation criteria listed in Section 3.4: Evaluation Criteria. The City will rank all qualified proposals and may select a finalist group of Respondents to interview with City leadership, or may make a final selection without a finalist interview; the City may request additional formal responses or submissions from finalists for clarification or to amplify proposal materials, but is not required to request clarification. Price proposals cannot be altered or modified as part of clarification.

Price proposals cannot be altered or modified as part of clarification. After the evaluation process, the City will make award(s) based on the evaluation and notify Respondents via email. Award to one Respondent does not mean other proposals lacked merit; the selected proposal was deemed most advantageous and the best value to the City, all factors considered. All Respondents will be notified of the status of their qualified proposal by the date of the proposed contract award in the schedule.

The City will assess individual submissions based on the Respondent's overall capabilities, experience, and the information provided in each response. Respondents found technically unqualified or whose submissions are deemed noncompliant will not be considered. Consultants responding to the RFP will be evaluated using four weighted criteria: 45% Response to project goals and scope; 25% Technical support during software implementation and ongoing; 20% Fee proposal and implementation schedule; 10% Information, qualifications, and references.

The RFP serves two purposes: (1) to inform potential respondents of the requirements and parameters of the software solution sought by the City, and (2) to set forth the terms of the resulting contract in conjunction with other specified documents. All terms in the RFP are enforceable as contract conditions in line with the General Contract Terms and Conditions; phrases such as "shall," "must," and "requirements" establish binding contractual obligations. When evaluating or rejecting proposals, the City will consider the extent to which respondents' solutions address the City's needs as outlined in the RFP. Unless explicitly stated otherwise, no single requirement automatically disqualifies a respondent, but non-compliance with any individual requirement may lead the City to exercise its discretion to reject a proposal in its entirety.

Section 4.0 of the RFP covers proposal requirements and the procedure for submitting proposals. By submitting a proposal, the Respondent agrees to meet all requirements in this section plus any other specifications, requirements, and terms and conditions stated in the RFP. Respondents with questions about a requirement or specification, or who believe modifying a requirement could improve the proposal to the City, are encouraged to submit these items as questions during the question and answer period per Section 2.3.

Proposal format rules: one (1) signed original hard copy plus one (1) digital version (e.g., Adobe Acrobat PDF); proposals must not exceed 20 pages, with an additional two (2) pages allowed for the cover letter and five (5) pages for appendices. Proposals must be organized in the specified order, with content requirements detailed in Section 4.2 PROPOSAL CONTENTS. Digital copy and all attachments must be emailed to accounting@colfax-ca.gov by August 28, 2025, at 4:00 PM PST with subject line "Accounting and Financial Software Submission". Original hard copy must be received by the same deadline at Attn: Shanna Stahl, City of Colfax, PO Box 702, Colfax, CA 95713 (USPS) or 33 S. Main Street, Colfax, CA 95713 (other delivery). Late proposals will not be considered or evaluated, and FAX submissions will not be accepted.

Proposals submitted by facsimile (FAX) will not be accepted. Respondents should regularly check the City's website at www.colfax-ca.gov for any addenda issued before the proposal deadline; all Respondents are considered to have read and understood all RFP information and addenda. Proposals may be withdrawn in writing by the office issuing the RFP before the proposal opening time stated on the cover page (or later if specified in an addendum); withdrawal requests must be on the Respondent's letterhead, signed by an authorized agent. Withdrawals after proposal opening are allowed only for good cause and at the City's discretion.

Section 4.2 "Proposal Contents" of the RFP requires respondents' proposals to include the required elements outlined in the RFP. Proposals must populate all attachments of this RFP that require information. An authorized signature must be included where requested. Additional details required for each proposal section are stated to be included below.

Tab 1 of the proposal requires respondents to address their approach to meeting the proposal goals and producing the deliverables outlined in Section 5.0, and encourages suggestions to improve implementation and utilization of the software and technical support approach. Specific required elements: submission of a completed "Software Abilities and Requirements" spreadsheet included as Attachment F; identification of the types of licenses offered for different levels of use; description of account number customization abilities; identification of where/when additional applications or other vendors will be utilized to meet requirements; and an outline of the availability of virtual demos to view product capabilities.

Tab 2 of the proposal requires Respondents to describe their proposed strategy and technical approach to meet the scope of work requirements in Section 5. Required elements: an implementation plan and timeline for execution, with the City's goal of going live on July 1, 2026, in coordination with the new fiscal year; description of levels of support for implementation; description of levels of support for recurring licenses and services; identification of key personnel for implementation; identification of training for software for different license levels, indicating whether training is in person, virtual, or standard recordings; and description of the proposed client engagement approach, including the use of an account manager.

The chunk is part of Tab 3: Firm Information and Qualifications under Section 4.2 Proposal Contents. It states that if multiple firms are responding as a team, the firm information shall be listed for each company.

Tab 3.1 Organization Information of the proposal requires: firm name, address, phone, website, and primary contact name, title and contact information; firm history, state of organization or incorporation, number of full-time employees, and type of ownership; hours of operation project managers will be available for technical assistance; office location(s) (City, State) from which key team individuals will operate. Proposers must also describe how their firm or team responds to the City's desire for participation by businesses owned by minorities, women, disabled, disabled business enterprises, and small businesses.

Tab 3.2 "Firm Qualifications and Experience" requires respondents to include recent relevant experience with project location and description, key staff who worked on the projects, and how results or effectiveness were measured. Required experience areas: implementing accounting and financial software for local governments, regional councils of government, or other federal grant-funded organizations; advising clients on streamlining procedures to improve organizational efficiency; and providing continued support for improvements and/or daily operations. Respondents must complete and submit Attachment B: References Sheet (may be recreated if content remains unchanged). If possible, the City prefers at least one local referral who is available for an in-person software demonstration.

Tab 3.3 requires a summary of qualifications for key personnel and any subcontractors proposed to provide services to the City under the proposed scope of work. Attachment A (Pricing Proposal) must state the total cost to the City for all services including materials, supplies and travel; the City will not accept unlimited reimbursable expenses, so any reimbursable expenses must be capped in the price proposal. Attachment A serves as a cover sheet, with the price proposal format at the Respondent's discretion but referencing the specific tasks and deliverables in Section 5, including: implementation fee and recurring fees broken out in detail; breakout of license fees; additional fees for support services with costs during implementation separated from post-implementation; and estimate of costs/fees for additional applications and/or vendors. Attachment B (References) requires a minimum of three (3) references for similar services, with valid e-mail addresses, and failure to provide a valid email may subject the proposal to rejection. Attachment C (Location of Workers Utilized by Respondent) requires detailing the location(s) where performance will occur and how resources or workers outside the United States will be utilized, which the City will evaluate for additional risks, costs and other factors before making an award. Attachment D is a Certification of Financial Condition.

The RFP requires several attachments with the proposal: Attachment D, Certification of Financial Condition, in which each Respondent certifies it is financially stable and able to complete the scope of work, and must notify the City within thirty (30) days of any occurrence or condition that materially alters the truth of any statement in the Certification from the date of Certification to Contract expiration. Attachment E, Certificate of Insurance, requires proof of insurance for the type of work solicited, including but not limited to workers compensation and commercial general liability coverage. Attachment F, Software Abilities and Requirements, requires completing an attached Excel spreadsheet (a separate document provided by the City) and returning it with the submission. Attachment G, Software Application Requirements, requires documentation demonstrating measures in place for protecting financial data and the secure access controls implemented.

Task 4 (Ongoing Technical Assistance & Support): automated updates and software change communications; support for annual e-filing such as 1099s and W-2s; help desk or ticketing system for support prioritization.

The City plans to start the project soon after awarding the contract and finalizing negotiations. The goal is to complete implementation by July 1, 2026, for the new fiscal year. Respondents should provide a proposed timeline and task sequence based on their expertise.
